contrast_detail: attended-auditory tones: infrequent (target) vs frequent (standard); frequent subsampled to target count per subject
note: active-task generalization cohort, erasure diagnostic only; NOT part of the 2x2 panel; 3rd consensus-marker family (auditory P300)
preprocess: preprocess_v2_events (~58 min run -> ICA+ICLabel+autoreject+CAR, bandpass 0.5-45, notch 60); 1 s post-stimulus trial windows
caveats: 1 s post-stimulus window = 200 samples = 1 patch, the shortest/minimal-context window of any cohort (auditory ERP is intrinsically brief). SOA median ~0.73 s so windows may overlap a following stimulus; the locked P300 still dominates.
frequent (standard) class subsampled to the target count per subject (oddball is ~20% of tones); without balancing the 1:4 skew + 0.5 threshold collapses BA.
P300 decoding from frozen FM features is unproven; a sub-gate (n.i.) result is an honest boundary finding, not a failure.
subj-BA chance floor 1/n_subj differs across cohorts; use subj-BA/chance ratio.
post-erasure label BA reaches 0.98-1.00 (ceiling) for all 3 FMs; Delta_erase magnitude is NOT a clean cross-cohort effect size here (erased side saturated).

raw (pre-erasure) label BA is already high (0.74-0.86): the P300 is strongly decodable even with subject variance present, so subject-identity 'masking' is milder than in the arithmetic/motor cohorts; erasure pushes an already-decodable signal to ceiling rather than rescuing a masked one.
subject BA pre (0.66-0.77) is lower than the 4-5 s cohorts (0.87-0.99): a 1 s window carries less subject identity, as expected.
